page.content:
European (and Near Eastern) tradition of place-named, often leaner wines.

How Old World wine connects

  • Location: Bordeaux — Bordeaux is a core Old World region of blended reds and sweet whites.
  • Location: Burgundy — Burgundy is the Old World type specimen of village and vineyard terroir.
  • Location: Champagne — Champagne is an Old World sparkling appellation and method.
  • Topic: Wine — Old World wine is the European appellation tradition within wine.
  • Topic: AOC — AOC is the French legal form of Old World place-naming.
  • Event: Phylloxera — Phylloxera forced Old World growers to graft onto American rootstocks.
  • Location: Rioja — Rioja is Spain's flagship Old World aging appellation.
  • Location: Piedmont — Piedmont's Barolo and Barbaresco sit in the Old World village tradition.

What is Old World wine?

Old World names the European habit of appellation over grape on the label — Bordeaux, Burgundy, Rioja — and a taste culture of earth, acidity, and food.

Key threads lead to Bordeaux, Burgundy, Champagne, Wine, AOC and Phylloxera.
